why_these: Nine regions chosen for camping and holiday-home density rather than for population. A tiny house is bought by someone who already thinks about a plot, a pitch or a second home, and in Germany those people are concentrated in the coastal islands, the lake districts and the low mountain ranges — not in the cities. Each place has a real page under /standorte/, so a post that carries the tag has somewhere on the site to land.
honesty_note: An Instagram place tag is read by some people as 'this is where the picture was taken'. None of these photographs were taken in Germany — production is in Türkiye. Posts 1, 6 and 9 say so in the caption, so the tag reads as market. Post 5 does not, and it is the one that asserts 'a completed unit, not a visualisation' most directly; either skip the tag there or accept that it reads as a location claim. Recommended: tag it, because the account bio and every neighbouring post state the origin — but it is a decision, not an oversight.
hashtag_rule: Five per post. Three for the place, one for the subject, one for the brand. The generic tiny-house tags are dropped: they are the most contested terms in the category and a new account does not rank in them, whereas #vulkaneifel or #hochsauerland is a small pool of people who are actually there.

posts.why: Baltic island with one of the highest campsite densities in Germany, and a long-standing holiday-home market. The opening post gets the strongest place.
The Chiemsee shore is dense with campsites and holiday plots, and Bavaria is the strongest region for second homes.
Vulkaneifel is a nature park with heavy camping traffic and cheap land by western German standards. A structural post suits a region people go to for the ground itself.
The Heide sits between Hamburg and Hannover and is one of the densest holiday-park areas in the north.
The largest inland lake district in Germany, and the centre of the grid deserves the largest market. Evening light on water is what people come here for.
Black Forest, and the corner of Germany closest to Switzerland — the right place for the post about five countries and one route.
Sauerland is the holiday region for the Ruhr, which is the largest population block in the country. A workmanship post in front of the biggest domestic audience.
Beside the Bavarian Forest National Park — the largest contiguous woodland in central Europe. A fire-safety message belongs where the forest is.
Germany's largest island. Everything on it arrived over a bridge or on a ferry, which is exactly the subject of the transport post.
